stem: In the school lab, Kavya makes a single slit narrower. Then she slides a third polaroid at 45° between two crossed polaroids lit by unpolarised light of intensity I0. What does she observe?

options.A: Central maximum gets narrower; I0/8 gets through the polaroids
options.B: Central maximum gets wider; no light gets through the polaroids
options.C: Central maximum gets wider; I0/8 gets through the polaroids
options.D: Central maximum gets wider; I0/4 gets through the polaroids

r1.text: A polaroid only blocks light, so putting one more in can't make the dark side bright.

r2.text: A thin slit spreads light more because width is 2λD/a, and the middle polaroid turns the light so some passes both.

r3.text: Less gap squeezes the light, so the bright band also gets thinner.

calc: Width = 2λD/a rises as a falls; I = (I0/2)·cos²45°·cos²45° = (I0/2)(1/2)(1/2) = I0/8
verify_flags: Ideal polaroids assumed (no absorption beyond Malus's law)
Option D slip = cos instead of cos²: (I0/2)·cos45°·cos45° = I0/4

stem: At a Pune science fair, Rohan narrows a razor-blade slit in front of a laser pointer. His friend Sana slips a polaroid at 45° between two crossed polaroids taped over a torch. What changes?

options.A: Laser's central bright patch shrinks; torch side lights up a little
options.B: Central bright patch spreads out; torch side lights up a little
options.C: Central bright patch spreads out; torch side stays dark
options.D: Central bright patch vanishes; torch becomes as bright as with no sheets

r1.text: Smaller gap means smaller patch, the light just comes out thinner.

r2.text: The crossed sheets already block everything, and a sheet can only block more.

r3.text: The narrow slit bends light out more, and the tilted sheet turns the light so part of it gets past the last sheet.

stem: Ananya's single slit (λ = 600 nm, screen 1.5 m away, a = 0.12 mm) gives a 15 mm central band. She narrows it to a = 0.06 mm and slips a 45° polaroid between two crossed ones. Which is right?

options.A: Central band 7.5 mm; one-eighth of the incoming unpolarised light now passes
options.B: Central band 30 mm; the crossed pair still passes no light
options.C: Central band 30 mm; one-quarter of the incoming unpolarised light now passes
options.D: Central band 30 mm; one-eighth of the incoming unpolarised light now passes

r1.text: Width is 2λD/a so halving a doubles it to 30 mm, and half, then half, then half again gives one-eighth.

r2.text: Half the slit, half the band, so 15 becomes 7.5 mm.

r3.text: Crossed means zero, and adding a sheet can't bring light back.

verify_flags: Check: 2(600e-9)(1.5)/(0.12e-3) = 0.015 m = 15 mm for the original slit

stem: At a Kochi exhibition, Neha narrows a slit in front of a laser. She also holds two polaroid sunglass lenses crossed in 64 W/m² of sunlight and slides a third lens at 45° between them. What does she find?

options.A: Laser's central band widens; 8 W/m² gets through the lenses
options.B: Laser's central band narrows; 8 W/m² gets through the lenses
options.C: Laser's central band widens; still 0 W/m² gets through the lenses
options.D: Laser's central band widens; 16 W/m² gets through the lenses

r1.text: Thin slit bends light more so the band widens, and 64 halves to 32, then ×½ and ×½ at the two 45° turns gives 8.

r2.text: A narrower slit lets through a narrower beam, so the band on the wall shrinks.

r3.text: Lenses are filters, a third one can only cut more light, so it stays zero.

calc: I = (64/2)·cos²45°·cos²45° = 32 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 8 W/m²; width 2λD/a grows as a shrinks
verify_flags: Sunlight treated as unpolarised and sunglass lenses as ideal polaroids
Option D slip = forgot the first lens halves unpolarised light: 64 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 16 W/m²
